```mermaid
graph TD
    A[User Authentication] --> B{Valid Credentials?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Create JWT Token]
    B -->|No| D[Return Error]
    C --> E[Store Token]
    E --> F[User Access Granted]
```

```mermaid
graph LR
    G[Create Todo] --> H{Validation Passes?}
    H -->|Yes| I[Save to Database]
    H -->|No| J[Return Error]
    I --> K[Update History]
```

## Critical Compliance Summary

| Requirement | Type | Enforced | Failure Consequence |
|-------------|------|----------|---------------------|
| Data Isolation | Privacy | Strict | HTTP 403 Forbidden |
| Password Policies | Security | Mandatory | Account lock after 5 failed attempts |
| Audit Logging | Security | Comprehensive | 90-day log retention |
| Todo Deletion | Privacy | Complete | All user data removed permanently |
| Pagination | Performance | Standard | HTTP 400 for invalid requests |

# Multi-User Todo Application

## 1. Service Overview

The Multi-User Todo Application is a private task management service enabling individual users to create, manage, and organize their personal to-do lists with rich features including editing history, trash management, and comprehensive filtering options. The service provides a secure, private environment where users can manage tasks without any possibility of cross-user data exposure.

### 1.1 Service Vision

Enable seamless personal task management with enterprise-grade features while ensuring strict data privacy. The application provides a clean, intuitive interface for managing to-dos with history tracking, flexible sorting, and robust privacy controls.

### 1.2 Problem Definition

Traditional todo apps either lack comprehensive privacy controls or have limited organizational features. This application solves the problem of personal task management with strict user isolation and full edit history tracking - crucial for users who need to maintain personal productivity systems without sharing or collaborating with others.

### 1.3 Core Value Proposition

- **Complete privacy**: No access to other users' data under any circumstances
- **Full edit history**: Track changes to todos with detailed timestamps and modifications
- **Flexible organization**: Sorting, filtering, and trash functionality
- **User control**: Complete management over account and data lifecycle

## 2. Business Model

### 2.1 Why This Service Exists

Personal task management is a fundamental productivity need with limited high-quality options that respect user privacy. This service addresses the gap between consumer-focused apps that monetize user data and enterprise tools that are overly complex for personal use.

### 2.2 Revenue Strategy

The service follows a freemium model:
- **Free tier**: Up to 500 todos with basic features
- **Premium tier**: $2.99/month for 10k todo limit, advanced filters, and priority support

### 2.3 User Acquisition Plan

- Content marketing targeting productivity bloggers
- Referral program for free tier users
- Integration with popular productivity tools (not directly implemented in app)

### 2.4 Success Metrics

- User retention rate > 75% after 30 days of usage
- 50% of free users upgrade to premium within first 6 months
- Avg. todo creation rate of 1.2 todos/user/day

## 3. User Actors and Authentication

### 3.1 Core Authentication Functions

WHEN a user signs up, THE system SHALL:
- Generate an email verification token for the provided address
- Store the user's password as a salted hash
- Create a user profile with a default display name of "User [UUID]"
- Send verification email with unique activation link

WHEN a user logs in with valid credentials, THE system SHALL:
- Issue a JWT access token with 15-minute expiration
- Issue a refresh token with 30-day expiration
- Return both tokens in the response
- Include the user ID in the token payload

### 3.2 Permission Matrix

| Feature                | User Role (Member) | Guest |
|------------------------|-------------------|-------|
| Create Todo            | Allowed           | Deny  |
| View Own Todos         | Allowed           | Deny  |
| Edit Todo              | Allowed           | Deny  |
| View/Edit Profile      | Allowed           | Deny  |
| Trash Management       | Allowed           | Deny  |
| View Other Users' Todos| Denied            | Deny  |
| Account Deletion       | Allowed           | Deny  |

### 3.3 Token Management

- Access tokens must be sent in Authorization header: "Bearer <token>"
- Refresh tokens shall be used only for obtaining new access tokens
- Token invalidation occurs when password is changed or account is deleted
- Automatic token refresh shall be provided via the /refresh endpoint

## 4. Functional Requirements Overview

### 4.1 Todo Management

The system must support comprehensive todo lifecycle management including:
- Creation with required title and optional details
- Completion toggle (complete/incomplete)
- Detailed editing capabilities
- Full history tracking

### 4.2 User Profile

Profiles are private and contain only display name, which users can edit. No fields are shared with other users.

### 4.3 Authentication

All endpoints must require authentication, with error responses for unauthorized access.

### 4.4 Privacy Rules

All data must be strictly isolated by user. No data leakage between users under any conditions.

## 5. User Scenarios

### 5.1 New User Onboarding

WHEN a new user registers with valid email and password,
THE system SHALL create the user account and send a verification email.

WHEN a user clicks the verification link,
THE system SHALL activate the account and direct to the todo creation interface.

WHEN a user provides incomplete registration data,
THE system SHALL return clear validation errors for required fields.

### 5.2 Core Todo Management

WHEN a user creates a todo with only the title,
THE system SHALL create the todo as incomplete with default dates (null)

WHEN a user marks a todo as complete,
THE system SHALL update the completion status and record the timestamp.

WHEN the user views their todo list,
THE system SHALL return paginated results with titles, completion status, and dates.

### 5.3 Editing Workflow

WHEN a user edits any todo field,
THE system SHALL create a new history entry recording the change.

WHEN the user views a todo's history,
THE system SHALL display the entries sorting from most recent to oldest.

### 5.4 Trash Management

WHEN a user deletes a todo,
THE system SHALL move it to the trash without removing from the database.

WHEN a user restores a todo from trash,
THE system SHALL return it to the active todo list.

WHEN a user permanently deletes a todo from trash,
THE system SHALL remove the todo and its entire history from the database.

## 6. Todo Creation Requirements

### 6.1 Title and Description

THE system SHALL require a title field (maximum 150 characters) during todo creation.

WHEN the title exceeds 150 characters,
THE system SHALL reject the request with error code TODO_TITLE_TOO_LONG.

THE system SHALL allow description up to 2000 characters, with empty value as valid.

### 6.2 Start and Due Dates

THE system SHALL accept dates in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD) for start and due dates.

WHEN the start date is after the due date,
THE system SHALL reject the request with error code TODO_DATE_ORDER_INVALID.

WHEN the due date has passed without completion,
THE system SHALL display a visual indicator (e.g., red color) for overdue todos.

### 6.3 Initial State

NEW todos SHALL default to incomplete status.

WHEN a user creates a todo with no start or due dates,
THE system SHALL store as NULL in the database.

### 6.4 Validation Rules

THE system SHALL validate all date fields against the ISO 8601 format when provided.

WHEN a user submits invalid dates, THE system SHALL return appropriate error messages.

## 7. Todo Edit History Requirements

### 7.1 History Entry Structure

EACH history entry SHALL contain:
- Timestamp of the edit
- Previous title (if changed)
- New title (if changed)
- Previous description (if changed)
- New description (if changed)
- Previous start date (if changed)
- New start date (if changed)
- Previous due date (if changed)
- New due date (if changed)

### 7.2 Sorting and Display

THE system SHALL sort history entries by timestamp descending.

WHEN the history list returns a large number of entries,
THE system SHALL paginate the results with maximum 25 entries per page.

### 7.3 Edit Validation

THE system SHALL not allow an edit if the todo has been permanently deleted.

WHEN a user tries to edit a completed todo, THE system SHALL allow the edit and reset completion status if the edit requires it.

## 8. Trash and Permanent Deletion Requirements

### 8.1 Trash View

THE system SHALL provide a separate endpoint for viewing trash contents.

WHEN a user accesses the trash list,
THE system SHALL return paginated items with title, original created date, and deletion date.

### 8.2 Restoration Process

WHEN a user restores a todo from trash,
THE system SHALL return it to the active list with the most recent state.

WHEN a todo is restored, THE system SHALL set completion status to previous value (not necessarily incomplete).

### 8.3 Permanent Deletion

WHEN a user permanently deletes a todo from trash,
THE system SHALL delete both the todo and its entire edit history.

THE system SHALL require explicit user confirmation before permanent deletion.

## 9. Privacy and Security Requirements

### 9.1 Data Isolation

THE system SHALL implement strict user data isolation where:
- Each user can access only their own todos
- All database queries must contain the current user ID as a filter
- API responses must not include any user ID in todo list responses

WHEN a user attempts to access another user's data, THE system SHALL return HTTP 403 Forbidden with error code USER_NOT_AUTHORIZED.

### 9.2 Authentication Security

THE system SHALL store passwords using bcrypt with a work factor of 12.

THE system SHALL implement rate limiting for authentication endpoints (100 attempts per minute per user).

### 9.3 Password Policies

THE system SHALL require passwords to be at least 12 characters long and include:
- One uppercase letter
- One lowercase letter
- One number
- One special character

WHEN a user changes their password, THE system SHALL log the change with timestamp and device information.

### 9.4 Audit Logging

THE system SHALL log all significant actions:
- Todo creation, updates, deletion
- User account modifications
- Authentication events
- Security incidents

Logs SHALL include:
- Timestamp
- User ID
- Action type
- Details of the action
- IP address of the request

## 10. Performance and Constraints

### 10.1 Performance Metrics

- Average response time for core todo operations: <1.5 seconds
- 95th percentile response time for paginated queries: <2.2 seconds
- API throughput: 100 requests per second per user

### 10.2 Data Limits

THE system SHALL permit a maximum of 10,000 todos per user account.

WHEN a user reaches 9,500 todos, THE system SHALL display a notification indicating the approaching limit.

WHEN a user attempts to create a new todo beyond the limit, THEN THE system SHALL reject with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests and error code TODO_LIMIT_REACHED.

### 10.3 Error Handling

WHEN a user provides invalid credentials, THE system SHALL return HTTP 401 Unauthorized with error code AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS.

WHEN a user attempts to access another user's data, THE system SHALL return HTTP 403 Forbidden with error code USER_NOT_AUTHORIZED.

WHEN a todo ID does not exist, THE system SHALL respond with HTTP 404 Not Found containing TODO_NOT_FOUND.

### 10.4 System Constraints

THE system SHALL NOT use server-side rendering.

THE system SHALL implement rate limiting on all authenticated endpoints (100 requests per minute per user).

WHILE under heavy load, THE system SHALL gracefully degrade to read-only mode.

THE system SHALL use JWT tokens with 15-minute access token and 30-day refresh token expiration.

NO external APIs shall be integrated for core functionality.

## Mermaid Diagrams

### Todo Creation Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    User->>Application: Submit Todo Creation
    Application->>Validation: Validate Title
    Validation-->>Application: Validated
    Application->>Database: Store Todo (incomplete)
    Database-->>Application: Success
    Application->>Response: Return Todo
```

### Todo Deletion and Recovery Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    User->>Application: Delete Todo
    Application->>Validation: Validate Todo Ownership
    Validation-->>Application: Validated
    Application->>Database: Log Deletion, Soft Delete
    Database-->>Application: Success
    User->>Application: View Trash
    Application->>Database: Query Deleted Todos
    Database-->>Application: List
    Application->>User: Show Trash List
    User->>Application: Restore Todo
    Application->>Validation: Check Trash Status
    Validation-->>Application: Valid
    Application->>Database: Undelete Todo
    Database-->>Application: Success
    Application->>User: Return to Active List
```

### User Authentication Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[User] -->|Sign Up| B(Create Account)
    B --> C{Send Verification Email}
    C -->|User Clicks Link| D[Activate Account]
    D --> E[Login]
    E -->|Valid Credentials| F[Issue Tokens]
    F --> G[Return Tokens]
    A -->|Login| H[Validate Credentials]
    H --> I[Issue Tokens]
    I --> G
```

This document serves as the authoritative requirements specification for the Multi-User Todo Application backend development team.

Database schema design:

Users table:
- id: UUID (primary key)
- email: TEXT (unique, not null)
- password_hash: TEXT (not null)
- display_name: TEXT
- created_at: TIMESTAMP
- updated_at: TIMESTAMP

Todos table:
- id: UUID (primary key)
- user_id: UUID (foreign key to Users.id, ON DELETE CASCADE)
- title: TEXT (not null)
- description: TEXT
- start_date: TIMESTAMP
- due_date: TIMESTAMP
- is_complete: BOOLEAN (default false)
- created_at: TIMESTAMP
- updated_at: TIMESTAMP
- deleted_at: TIMESTAMP (nullable for soft delete)

TodoHistory table:
- id: UUID (primary key)
- todo_id: UUID (foreign key to Todos.id, ON DELETE CASCADE)
- timestamp: TIMESTAMP
- title: TEXT
- description: TEXT
- start_date: TIMESTAMP
- due_date: TIMESTAMP
- created_at: TIMESTAMP

Relationships:
- Users has many Todos (ON DELETE CASCADE)
- Todos has many TodoHistory (ON DELETE CASCADE)
- Soft delete implemented via deleted_at field in Todos table

### `todo_app_users`

User accounts with email/password credentials, verification status, and
display name. Serves as the primary identity record for all
authentication flows and permission structures. All business operations
related to user accounts originate from this model.

Key relationships:
- Governed by session table: todo_app_user_sessions
- Manages password reset tokens via: todo_app_user_password_resets
- Handles email verification via: todo_app_user_email_verifications
- User-owned todos tracked through: todo_app_todos table

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Registered email address used for account identification. Must be unique
  > across all user accounts.
- `password_hash`: Securely hashed password representation. Never stores plaintext passwords.
- `display_name`
  > User's customizable display name visible to other users. Max 30
  > characters.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the user account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when user profile was last modified.

### `todo_app_user_sessions`

JWT session tokens with access and refresh capabilities for authenticated
user sessions.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_user_id`: The user associated with this session.
- `ip`: IP address used during login.
- `href`: Current URL of the session.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL for the session.
- `created_at`: Session creation time.
- `expired_at`: Session expiration time.

### `todo_app_user_password_resets`

Password reset tokens with 15-minute expiration and usage tracking.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_id`
  > The user associated with this password reset token. {@link
  > todo_app_users.id}.
- `token`: The unique password reset token for user account restoration.
- `expires_at`: Expiration timestamp in UTC. Valid for 15 minutes from token creation.
- `used_at`
  > Timestamp when the reset token was used to successfully update the
  > password.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this password reset record was created.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this password reset record was last updated (e.g., expiry
  > reset).
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when this password reset record was soft deleted.

### `todo_app_user_email_verifications`

Email verification tokens with expiration for registration completion.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_id`: User who requested email verification. [todo_app_users.id](#todo_app_users)
- `token`: Unique verification token for email validation.
- `expires_at`: Expiration timestamp of the verification token.

### `todo_app_histories`

Audit log of all todos' edit history, capturing field changes including
title, description, start date, and due date. Each history entry
references the corresponding todo and stores the timestamp of the edit.
Maintains temporal data including creation and update times, with
optional soft deletion support for the history entry itself.

Properties as follows:

### `todo_app_todos`

User-owned todo records with title, status, dates, and soft-delete tracking.

This table represents the core business entity for todo management,
allowing users to create, filter, sort, and manage their todos with full
soft-delete support. All todos are bound to a single user via user_id
foreign key. The table maintains historical state through soft-deletion
and is intended for independent CRUD operations via API endpoints.

- `is_complete`: Completion status (default false)
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (null for active records)

API specification design:

Endpoints:

Authentication:
- POST /auth/register (create user account)
- POST /auth/login (user authentication)
- PUT /auth/password (change password)
- DELETE /auth (delete user account, including todos)

User Profile:
- GET /profile (get display name)
- PUT /profile (update display name)

Todos:
- POST /todos (create new todo)
- GET /todos (list todos with pagination, filtering, sorting)
- GET /todos/:id (get single todo details)
- PUT /todos/:id (update todo details)
- PATCH /todos/:id/complete (toggle completion status)
- DELETE /todos/:id (soft delete todo)

Trash:
- GET /trash (list deleted todos)
- POST /trash/:id/restore (restore from trash)
- DELETE /trash/:id (permanent delete from trash)

Todo History:
- GET /todos/:id/history (view edit history)

Request/Response Structures:
- All endpoints require authentication (JWT)
- All "todos" endpoints operate on current user's todos
- Pagination parameters: page (default 1), limit (default 10)
- Filtering: filter by completion status (all, complete, incomplete)
- Sorting: sortBy (creationDate|startDate|dueDate), order (asc|desc)
- Time fields (start_date, due_date) should use ISO 8601 format
- Soft delete implemented via "deleted_at" field
- All "id" parameters are UUID format
- Response structures must include all required fields from requirements
- Error responses should follow standard format (400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, etc.)

operations.specification: Create new user account with email, password, and default display name. Securely hash password, send welcome email, set verification status to 'pending', and generate JWT access/refresh tokens. Validate email format and password requirements before account creation.
operations.description:
This endpoint creates a new user account in the system. The request requires a valid email address formatted as per standard email policies and a password meeting the minimum length requirement of 12 characters. The system validates the email format, checks password strength, securely hashes the password using industry-standard algorithms, and establishes a new user record with a pending verification status.

The user's display name is set to the email username (e.g., 'johnsmith' from 'johnsmith@example.com'). A welcome email with account confirmation instructions is sent to the provided email address. Upon successful account creation, the system returns JWT access and refresh tokens for authentication. The user must complete email verification before gaining full access to application features.

This implementation ensures all security requirements are met including password hashing, email verification, and secure token generation. The operation complies with privacy requirements by restricting personal data access to the user themselves.

operations.specification: Validate user credentials and generate JWT tokens for authenticated sessions. Check email/password against database records, verify account status, and generate both access and refresh tokens. Enforce session management rules and token rotation.
operations.description:
This endpoint authenticates users by validating their credentials against the database. The request requires a valid email address and matching password to verify user identity. The system checks for active account status and email verification completion before granting access.

Upon successful validation, the system generates an access token with a standard expiration period and a refresh token with extended validity. The access token contains user ID and basic role information for authorization. The refresh token allows for token renewal without requiring user re-authentication.

Security considerations include preventing brute-force attacks through rate limiting and using secure token storage practices. The operation ensures all authentication activities are logged for audit purposes, and previous sessions are invalidated when a new session is created. The operation strictly follows the privacy requirements by ensuring credentials are never stored or transmitted in plaintext.

This endpoint refreshes the access token using a valid refresh token previously issued to the user. The request validates the refresh token against the database record to ensure it has not expired or been revoked. The system checks for active user session status and validates the token against the user's current session.

If valid, the system generates a new access token with extended expiration and keeps the refresh token unchanged for future use. This operation enables seamless user experience without requiring re-login while maintaining security through short-lived access tokens.

The refresh process maintains all security protocols including token rotation, session management, and audit logging. The operation complies with privacy requirements by ensuring no personal data is exposed during token refresh. The refresh token remains stored securely on the client side, and the system enforces refresh token expiration policies to prevent abuse.

The history is stored even after a todo is moved to trash, preserving a complete audit trail. By default, the operation returns the 20 most recent history entries sorted from newest to oldest.

All entries are scoped to the currently authenticated user, with appropriate ownership verification automatically enforced. No pagination parameters are required for the default behavior, but additional pages could be requested with pagination query parameters in future extensions.

operations.specification: Query the todo_app_todos table where deleted_at is not null, filtered by current user ID from authentication. Implement cursor-based pagination with default page 1, limit 10. Support filtering by completion status (all, complete, incomplete). Return todos with title, status, start_date, due_date, and creation_date fields. The response should include pagination metadata (total count, current page, page size).
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of soft-deleted todos in the trash.

This operation provides users with access to their deleted todos that are stored in the trash. The trash view displays all soft-deleted todos for the current user, with the same fields as the main todo list: title, completion status, start date, due date, and creation date.

Users can filter the trash items by completion status (all, complete, incomplete) or paginate through results. The endpoint is essential for managing deleted todos, allowing users to restore or permanently delete items from their trash.

All todos shown in the trash are owned by the authenticated user, with strict isolation enforced via the authentication system. The system will never return todos belonging to other users.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of trash items with summary information

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Service layer verifies user ownership of the todo by checking against authenticated user ID. Sets 'deleted_at' to null and resets completion status to INCOMPLETE. Preserves all historical edits (via todo_app_histories) without modification. Returns the fully restored todo entity with updated active state. Performs this as a single transaction to maintain data integrity.
operations.description:
Restore a todo item from the trash back to the active list.

This operation moves a previously soft-deleted todo from the trash view back to the primary todo list, making it visible in regular todo views. The restored todo retains all its edit history, original completion status, dates, and associated details.

The authenticated user must be the owner of the todo being restored (verified via user ID checks against the database). The completion status of the restored todo is reset to INCOMPLETE, matching the state it was in before being moved to trash.

All associated edit history entries (todo_app_histories) are preserved without modification, ensuring full audit trail visibility. This operation does not require any input data - only the target todo ID in the path parameter.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the todo to restore, must match the user's deleted todo

responseBody.description: Restored todo details including all original fields and history

operations.name: restore

operations.specification:
1. Verify user owns the todo in trash (via todo_app_todos.deleted_at IS NOT NULL)
2. Identify associated history entries (todo_app_histories.todo_id = id)
3. Delete all related history entries (todo_app_histories)
4. Permanently delete the todo record (todo_app_todos)
5. Return 204 No Content
6. Handle edge case: 404 if todo not found in trash
operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo item from the trash.

This endpoint allows users to purge a todo item that was previously marked as deleted (soft-deleted) from the system. When called, the todo and all associated edit history entries are permanently removed from the database with no possibility of restoration.

The operation requires that the todo must be currently in the trash state (soft-deleted) to be eligible for permanent deletion. Users can access this endpoint to clean up their trash and free up database storage.

Note: This action cannot be undone. It is designed for permanent cleanup of unnecessary trash items that have not been restored.

instruction:
E2E test strategies:

Authentication:
- Test register with valid/invalid email, password (400 for invalid)
- Test login with valid/invalid credentials (401 for invalid)
- Test password change with valid/invalid current password
- Test account deletion (verify todos permanently deleted)

User Profile:
- Test get profile (200), update display name (200 with confirmation)

Todos:
- Test list with pagination (page=1, limit=10), filtering (status: all/complete/incomplete), sorting (newest/oldest, start due dates)
- Test create todo (valid title, invalid with missing title 400)
- Test update (change title, description, dates - verify history)
- Test toggle completion (200 for both states)
- Test soft delete (200, moved to trash), verify history preserved
- Test restore (200, returns to active), test permanent delete from trash (200, history gone)

Edge Cases:
- Todos with missing dates during sorting (appear at end)
- Empty description field (valid)
- Pagination with large datasets
- Unauthorized access attempts (401 for every endpoint)

Error Handling:
- All endpoints return 400 for invalid input, 401 for unauthorized
- Ensure JWT token is used in all authenticated requests
- Verify response schemas match OpenAPI specifications

instruction:
Implement business logic for all API endpoints as specified in the interface agent output. Key implementation focus:

- Use Prisma to interact with database schema
- Implement authentication middleware (JWT)
- Handle soft delete via 'deleted_at' field
- Preserve edit history in TodoHistory table on every todo modification
- Implement pagination, filtering, and sorting as per API specification
- Ensure all operations are scoped to current user's data
- Validate all input parameters against DTO schemas
- Implement error handling for 400/401 responses
- Follow NestJS best practices for service layer organization
